summary: Master the art of knowledge curation in the digital workplace. Join our training course to improve your information management and collaboration skills.
lede: Knowledge curation in a digital workplace organizes information so people can find and reuse what they need. For professionals who work with information, content, and knowledge in digital tools, this involves mapping knowledge flows, structuring content with tags and metadata, and creating reusable guides, FAQs, and playbooks. Teams can also maintain content through review cycles and improve findability using search feedback and simple analytics.
audienceIntro: This course is specifically designed for professionals who regularly work with information, content, and knowledge in digital tools. It will enable you to streamline knowledge sharing and improve findability in your organization.
audience: Knowledge management or knowledge officer roles
Digital workplace, intranet, or collaboration platform owners
modules: Foundations of Knowledge Curation in the Digital Workplace
Mapping Knowledge Flows and Pain Points
Tools and Platforms for Knowledge Curation
Turning Tacit Know-how into Reusable Knowledge Assets
Culture, Collaboration, and Communities of Practice
Analytics, Feedback Loops, and Continuous Improvement
Implementing Your Knowledge Curation Action Plan
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of digital workplace tools and a role involving information management or collaboration. Familiarity with platforms like Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or similar is beneficial.
